title: Robinson Crusoe
author: d'après Daniel Defoe
desc: Seul survivant d'un naufrage, Robinson vit vingt-huit ans sur une île déserte.

p: Robinson Crusoe was a young Englishman who loved the sea. His father wanted him to study law, but Robinson only dreamed of adventures.
In 1659, he was sailing from Brazil to Africa when a terrible storm hit the ship. The waves were as big as mountains. The ship broke on the rocks.
Robinson was thrown into the sea. He swam and swam. A huge wave carried him to a beach. He was alive!
He looked around. There was nobody. All his companions were dead. He was alone on an unknown island.
That night, he slept in a tree, because he was afraid of wild animals. He had nothing. Only a knife, a pipe and a little tobacco.
The next morning, Robinson saw the ship. It was stuck on the rocks, not far from the beach. He swam to it.
For many days, he made a raft and brought things from the ship: food, tools, guns, gunpowder, clothes, ropes, even a dog and two cats.
He built a house in a cave, with a strong wall around it. He made a calendar with a big piece of wood. Every day, he cut a line in it, so he did not forget the date.
He learned to do everything himself. He grew corn and rice. He kept goats for milk and meat. He made pots from clay. He made clothes from goat skins and an umbrella against the sun.
Sometimes he was very sad and lonely. But he read his Bible and wrote in his diary. And slowly, he found peace.
After fifteen years on the island, Robinson walked on the beach one day, and he froze. There, in the sand, was the print of a human foot!
He ran home, terrified. Who was it? For two years, he lived in fear.
Then one day, he saw canoes on the beach, and men around a fire. They were cannibals from another island, and they had prisoners.
One of the prisoners escaped and ran toward Robinson's hill. Two men ran after him. Robinson came out with his gun and saved the young man.
The young man knelt down and put Robinson's foot on his head, to say: "I am yours, you saved my life."
It was a Friday. So Robinson called him Friday.
Robinson taught Friday English, and Friday taught Robinson many things about the island and the sea. They became true friends. For the first time in many years, Robinson laughed.
Together, they built a big canoe. Then, one day, an English ship arrived. The sailors had rebelled against their captain and wanted to leave him on the island.
Robinson and Friday helped the captain take back his ship. To thank them, the captain took them to England.
On the 19th of December 1686, Robinson Crusoe left his island. He had lived there for twenty-eight years, two months and nineteen days.

When he arrived in England, everything had changed. But Robinson had changed too. On the island, alone, he had learned the most important lesson: with courage and patience, a person can survive almost anything.
